subject.title: Feature Request: Add custom client display name for TUI

question: Should OpenClaw expose a user-facing TUI display-name override, and should the approved surface be a CLI-only `--client-name` flag, a persisted config setting, or an auto-derived label?
rationale: This adds a public CLI/config-adjacent surface and affects Gateway-visible presence metadata, so automation should not choose naming, persistence, validation, or privacy defaults without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add CLI-only opt-in flag
options.body: Add a bounded `openclaw tui --client-name <name>` path that only affects Gateway-mode presence for that process and keeps the existing default unchanged.

options.title: Add persisted TUI config
options.body: Add a canonical TUI config key if maintainers want a stable per-user default, with schema, docs, and tests covering explicit CLI precedence.

options.title: Defer display-name customization
options.body: Keep `openclaw-tui` as the only TUI label until a broader TUI identity and privacy policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Add CLI-only opt-in flag
recommendation.body: Add a bounded `openclaw tui --client-name <name>` path that only affects Gateway-mode presence for that process and keeps the existing default unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: This is mostly a public CLI/Gateway metadata product decision, and recent Gateway client API and TUI Gateway-path history point to this owner signal.
